question.text: An investor expects a significant move in bond prices but is uncertain about the direction. Which option strategy would best capitalize on this expected large move?

answer.text: Buy a straddle (buy both ATM call and ATM put) to profit from a large move in either direction
Sell a straddle to collect maximum premium from both options
Buy only an ATM call option, since rates are likely to fall
Stay out of the options market until the direction becomes clear

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes a long straddle -- buying a call and a put at the same strike and expiry -- as the strategy used when the direction is uncertain but a significant move is expected. Profit arises from a large move in either direction. The Trap: Selling a straddle profits from low realised volatility, which is the opposite of what is expected. Buying only a call takes a directional bet, contradicting the uncertainty about direction. Note: The long straddle pays off whenever the underlying moves enough -- up or down -- to cover the combined premium paid on the call and the put.
